tasks.title: Change calculator button colors by type
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: Add distinct background colors for operator buttons (+, -, ×, ÷), the clear button (C), the equals button (=), and keep digit buttons with their default style, so the calculator is visually easier to use.
2. READ FIRST: src/components/Button.css (existing button styles and CSS variable usage), src/components/Calculator.tsx (how buttons are rendered and className is passed), src/App.css (CSS variable definitions for :root and dark theme).
3. FILES: Modify src/components/Button.css to add new variant classes (.operator-button, .clear-button, .equals-button). Modify src/components/Calculator.tsx to assign the correct variant className based on the button label: operators (÷, ×, -, +) get 'operator-button', 'C' gets 'clear-button', '=' gets 'equals-button'. Pass these alongside the existing wide class logic.
4. APPROACH: In Calculator.tsx, create a helper function getButtonClass(label: string) that returns the appropriate extra class. Combine it with the existing wide-class logic: e.g., className={[label === '0' ? 'wide' : '', getButtonClass(label)].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}. In Button.css, add three new CSS rule blocks — .calculator-button.operator-button, .calculator-button.clear-button, .calculator-button.equals-button — each overriding background, border, and text color with concrete hex values (not CSS variables) so colors are visible in both themes. Suggested: operators = orange (#e67e22 to #d35400), clear = red (#e74c3c to #c0392b), equals = green (#27ae60 to #1e8449). Keep hover/active state rules consistent by also adding :hover overrides for each variant.
5. PATTERNS: Follow the existing .calculator-button style structure in Button.css. Follow the existing button map and className pattern in Calculator.tsx line 179-185. Write or update src/components/Button.test.tsx and src/components/Calculator.test.tsx to verify that operator buttons receive the 'operator-button' class, the clear button receives 'clear-button', the equals button receives 'equals-button', and digit buttons do not receive any of these classes.
acceptance_criteria: npx tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 (no TypeScript errors)
npm run build exits with code 0
Operator buttons (÷, ×, -, +) render with class 'operator-button' in the DOM
Clear button (C) renders with class 'clear-button' and equals button (=) renders with class 'equals-button'
